This tiny $1 chip connects things to the internet from 10 miles away

A LoRaWAN gateway can speak to tiny, battery-powered LoRaWAN (Long Range Wide-area network) sensors and gizmos from more than 10 miles away (line of sight) or within a few miles if obstructed by the walls of a building. It’s capable of a meager bi-directional data rate between 0.3 kbps and 50 kbps on either 433MHz, 868MHz (most of Europe), or 915MHz (USA) frequencies.

Yeah, but does it go through brick of cement walls? This was a major problem for my FRS walkies and for cell phones.

This could be tremendously good for monitoring pollution in all kinds of things like air and water.

So to get kilobytes, do I divide 50 kbps by 8? 50/8 = 6.25 kilobytes. Just fine for small pieces of data, like monitoring stations.

What about licensing issues in the US?

Depends on the freq setting. 433Mz penetrates very well, much better than cell phones (750-2100MHz). The freq selection is a trade off between range and bandwidth. 433 will reach out to 15km, but has half the bandwidth of the 868/915 frequencies.

All the operating frequencies are on ISM reserved spectrum the same as WiFi. They are unregulated bands so there are no licensing considerations. The flip side of the coin is that there transmit power limitations and no guarantee that the frequency will not encounter interference. Interference can be largely filtered out by a good protocol, but it costs additional signalling cycles, which again lowers bandwidth.

So you're not likely to surf the internet on these devices, but for automated messaging exchange this is an excellent system. With the price point down at $200 for a gateway and transceivers for $1 this has huge potential. Even as an independent tinkerer, it would be quite reasonable to install this as a backbone for home security and automation. The big potential is for regional network build outs though.

My big outstanding question is the security model. This is critical for both personal and network infrastructure use cases. I won't use it at home if I can't secure it. And I sure as hell won't be sending it over a regional network if I'm exposing my data to either network sniffing or operator inspection. FBI / NSA / TLOs will be all over this IMNSHO.
